whale-shark-season-seychelles.title: When can you swim with whale sharks in Seychelles?
whale-shark-season-seychelles.imageAlt: Snorkeler swimming alongside a whale shark in Seychelles
whale-shark-season-seychelles.metaTitle: Whale Shark Season Seychelles · When & Where to Swim with Them
whale-shark-season-seychelles.metaDescription: Whale sharks visit Seychelles from August to October. Best months, top spots, ethical guidelines, what to expect. Plan your swim with a private boat from La Digue.
whale-shark-season-seychelles.lead: The largest fish in the ocean swims through Seychelles waters every year. and the inner islands are one of the few places on Earth where you can snorkel with them without crowds. Here is everything you need to plan it.

sections.title: The whale shark season explained
sections.body:
Whale sharks (Rhincodon typus) follow plankton blooms across the western Indian Ocean. In Seychelles their main aggregation season runs from August to October. those three months are when sightings peak around Mahé and the inner islands. They are filter feeders, harmless to humans, and reach 8-12 metres in adult length. The animals you see are usually juvenile males between 4 and 8 metres long.

Outside that window. November to July. sightings exist but are rare and unpredictable. If swimming with a whale shark is the highlight of your trip, plan your travel inside the August-October bracket.

sections.title: Best months. and best weeks within them
sections.body:
September is the historical sweet spot. The plankton bloom is at its richest, the south-east trade winds have settled, and the visibility is excellent. often above 20 metres. October has more variable weather but higher densities of animals near the surface. August is the earliest reliable month and tends to be quieter on the water.

Within a given month, conditions change week to week. The best advice is to keep your dates flexible by 2-3 days and let the captain pick the window. We rebook free of charge if the day you booked turns out to be a low-probability one and a better day is available within 72 hours.

sections.title: Where they appear
sections.body:
The main aggregation zone is the deeper water off Mahé's west coast. between Beau Vallon and Anse Major. From La Digue we run the trip as a long day (10-11 hours) with a spotter on board and, when possible, coordination with the Marine Conservation Society Seychelles. Closer to home, we have occasional sightings at the drop-offs off Coco Island and around the south of Félicité. September-October only.

If you'd rather avoid the long crossing, we recommend basing the whale shark day out of Mahé. We can coordinate the transfer.

sections.title: What to expect. and how we do it ethically
sections.body:
A whale shark encounter is a snorkel, not a dive. You enter the water about 30 metres from the animal, fins on, mask cleared, and let it approach. The animal sets the pace. We never chase, never touch, never feed.

The Seychelles guidelines are clear: maximum 8 swimmers in the water at a time, minimum 3 metres from the head and 4 metres from the tail, no flash photography, no scuba diving in the immediate zone. Our captain enforces these rules. they're how the population stays habituated to swimmers year after year.

A typical encounter lasts 5 to 15 minutes per pass. On a good day you may have 3-5 passes with the same or different individuals. On a quiet day you may have none. the sea is not a zoo. We are honest about the day in the morning briefing.

sections.title: What to bring
sections.body: Reef-safe sunscreen, your own mask if you have one (we provide quality gear for those who don't), an underwater camera if you want photos (no flash), a long-sleeve rashguard for sun protection during the long boat ride out. We provide drinks, snacks and a hot lunch if the trip is extended.

faq.q: Is it safe to swim with whale sharks?
faq.a: Yes. whale sharks are filter feeders. They have no teeth that bite, no tail strike behaviour, no defensive aggression. The only risks are sunburn, dehydration, and your own enthusiasm carrying you too close. We brief on all three.

faq.q: How likely is a sighting in season?
faq.a: In September around Mahé, our hit rate is roughly 80% on a single day, ~95% on a 2-day attempt. August and October are 60-70%. Outside season we don't run dedicated trips.

faq.q: Can children participate?
faq.a: Confident swimmers of 10+ years old, yes. Below that we recommend the captain stays with the child near the boat while parents go in.

faq.q: Are there scuba options?
faq.a: Scuba is not permitted in the immediate snorkel zone (animal welfare regulation). Snorkel-only.

faq.q: Do I need a license or insurance?
faq.a: No license. Travel insurance covering watersports is recommended (most policies cover snorkeling by default).

faq.q: How long is the trip from La Digue?
faq.a: 10 to 11 hours door to door if we go to the main Mahé aggregation zone. From Praslin: 8 hours. Many guests prefer to base the trip out of Mahé. we can coordinate.

best-time-to-visit-seychelles.title: When is the best time to visit Seychelles?
best-time-to-visit-seychelles.imageAlt: Master Boat Charter at anchor under Seychelles sky
best-time-to-visit-seychelles.metaTitle: Best Time to Visit Seychelles · Month by Month Guide (2026)
best-time-to-visit-seychelles.metaDescription: Month-by-month weather, sea conditions, wildlife, and crowd levels in Seychelles. April-May and September-October are the sweet spots. here's why.
best-time-to-visit-seychelles.lead: Seychelles is good all year. but "good" varies. The wind shifts, the rain falls in different places, the sea changes colour. Two windows stand out for boat travellers: April-May and September-October. Here is the full month-by-month breakdown.

sections.title: The two monsoons that shape the year
sections.body:
Seychelles has two trade-wind seasons. The north-west monsoon runs roughly November to March. warmer air, more humidity, occasional heavy rain, calmer sea on the south-east coasts. The south-east monsoon runs May to September. drier, cooler nights, breezier days, choppier sea on the east coasts. Between the two are the transition months. April and October-November. which combine the best of both: warm, dry, calm.

For boat travel, this is the most important fact. Calm sea + good visibility + low rain = April, May, September, October.

sections.title: Month by month
sections.body:
**January.** Warm, humid, occasional heavy showers. Sea visibility variable. Lower tourist numbers; good for beach time and short boat trips. Whale sharks: not in season.

**February.** Similar to January. Hot. Some of the strongest rain of the year falls in short bursts. Inner-island snorkeling still works on the lee side.

**March.** Transition begins. Wind drops. Rain decreases. Last chance for the calmest waters before April. Excellent for sunset cruises.

**April.** One of the two best months. Hot, dry, sea like glass, visibility often above 25 metres. Crowds still moderate. Whale sharks not in season but everything else is at its best.

**May.** Trade winds settle. Slightly cooler at night. Inner-island snorkeling still excellent on the lee side. Good prices.

**June.** South-east wind picks up. East-coast beaches can get seaweed. Inner-island west-side spots stay excellent. Fishing season for sailfish opens.

**July.** Windier. Sea cooler. Big game fishing peaks. Inner-island sheltered snorkeling still good.

**August.** Wind eases off mid-month. Whale shark sightings begin. Big game fishing remains strong.

**September.** The other best month. Whale sharks at peak. Sea calming. Visibility excellent again. Slightly more tourists than April.

**October.** Wind drops further. Whale sharks still present early in the month. Excellent inner-island conditions. Honeymoon high season.

**November.** Transition into the north-west monsoon. Calm sea but some rain. Quieter on the water. Good value.

**December.** High season for European holidays. Warm, humid, occasional rain. Christmas/NYE bookings need 3+ months lead time.

sections.title: When to book for what you want
sections.body:
For a private boat day with maximum visibility: April, May, September, October.

For whale sharks: August (late) to October. September is the safest bet.

For big game fishing: June, July, August.

For honeymoons (calm sea + light + sunsets): April-May or October. Avoid late January-February (rain peak).

For families with young children: April-May (transition, calm) or November (similar, less expensive).

sections.title: What we do when the weather turns
sections.body:
Our cancellation policy is built around weather. If the captain calls it (safety, not preference), we refund or reschedule in full. If you call it, the 72-hour rule applies. In practice, we lose 5-10 days a year to weather across all seasons. usually rescheduled within 48 hours.

The inner islands are protected enough that the day is rarely completely cancelled. We adapt the route. east coast becomes west coast, full-day becomes half-day, snorkeling site shifts. The skill of the captain is mostly in this adaptation.

best-time-to-visit-seychelles.faqTitle: Best time to visit. frequently asked

faq.q: What's the absolute best month for a Seychelles boat trip?
faq.a: Late April or late September. April for the calmest sea before the south-east winds, September for the post-monsoon clarity and the whale sharks.

faq.q: Is Christmas/New Year a good time?
faq.a: Yes for atmosphere and warmth, but it's the highest-rain period and the most expensive. Book 4+ months ahead if that's your window.

faq.q: Are there cyclones in Seychelles?
faq.a: Seychelles sits outside the main cyclone tracks. direct hits are rare (last major one: 2018, Cyclone Berguitta brushed past). The country is considered cyclone-safe.

faq.q: When are prices lowest?
faq.a: May, early June, late October to mid-December are the quieter and cheaper windows. Our prices stay flat year-round but accommodation around the islands drops by 30-40% in these months.

faq.q: What's the water temperature?
faq.a: 26-29°C year-round. You don't need a wetsuit. A rashguard is helpful for long days in the sun.

curieuse-island.title: Curieuse Island. Giant Tortoises & Castaway Beaches
curieuse-island.tagline: Marine park · Aldabra tortoises · Anse Papaie
curieuse-island.lead: A private boat day to one of the most beloved inner islands of Seychelles. Aldabra giant tortoises on land, a protected coral marine park in the water, and a beach lunch where the only footprints are yours.
curieuse-island.imageAlt: Turquoise lagoon at Curieuse Island Marine Park, Seychelles
curieuse-island.metaTitle: Curieuse Island Tour Seychelles · Private Boat from La Digue
curieuse-island.metaDescription: Curieuse Island day tour from La Digue: Aldabra giant tortoises, marine park snorkeling, Anse Papaie beach BBQ, St-Pierre Islet stop. €175 / person, drinks & lunch included. Local Seychellois captain.
curieuse-island.schemaName: Curieuse Island Full-Day Private Boat Tour from La Digue

sections.title: Why Curieuse is the most rewarding day at sea in the inner islands
sections.body:
Curieuse is the rare Seychelles island where land, reef and history meet on a single afternoon. Once a leper colony, today it is a national park rebuilt around the reintroduction of Aldabra giant tortoises. over a hundred of them roam freely on the trails. The west coast is a protected marine park: shallow, clear, alive with parrotfish, butterflyfish and the occasional hawksbill turtle.

We spend the morning at anchor on the marine park side, drift over the reef on the changing tide, then beach the bow at Anse Papaie for a barbecue cooked by your captain while you walk the tortoise trail.

sections.title: What you'll see in the marine park
sections.body: Conditions permitting, we plan three snorkeling drops on this trip. Anse Saint-Joseph for the table corals and sergeant majors, the small bay below the ranger station for hawksbill turtles, and the southern point for a slow drift in 3-5 metres of glass-flat water. Bring a reef-safe sunscreen. we provide everything else.

sections.title: The barbecue on Anse Papaie
sections.body:
Anse Papaie is a tongue of white sand that you can only reach by boat. Lunch is grilled fish (kingfish, snapper or job depending on the day), salads, fresh fruit and Seybrew cold from the cooler. Soft drinks and water are included; if you'd like a specific drink, tell us when you book.

The beach is shared with a handful of land iguanas and the occasional tortoise that wanders out of the forest. It is one of the quietest beach lunches you can have in this archipelago.

sections.title: Combine Curieuse with St-Pierre Islet on the way home
sections.body: If the sea is calm, we add a snorkel stop at St-Pierre Islet on the return leg. a granite outcrop a kilometre off Anse Volbert with one of the densest concentrations of reef fish in the inner islands. It adds about 45 minutes to the day and is one of our most-requested extras.

curieuse-island.highlightsTitle: What's included in your Curieuse day
highlights: Private boat, no other group on board
Local Seychellois captain who knows every reef
Beach barbecue with grilled fish and salads
Marine park fee guidance (payable on arrival)

faq.q: Are the marine park fees included in the price?
faq.a: No. The Curieuse Marine Park fee is paid on arrival to the rangers (currently around €27 per adult, free for children under 12). Our captain handles the paperwork.

faq.q: Will we actually see the giant tortoises?
faq.a: Almost always. The tortoise sanctuary on Anse Saint-Joseph hosts more than 200 individuals. they roam freely. Some are over a hundred years old.

faq.q: Can we visit the Doctor's House and walk to Anse Saint-Joseph?
faq.a: Yes. The trail is gentle (about 30 minutes one way) and we time the lunch so you have an afternoon window for the walk if you wish.

faq.q: Is the trip suitable for children?
faq.a: Yes. the snorkeling sites are shallow and protected, the trail is family-friendly, and we provide life jackets in all sizes.

faq.q: What about seasickness?
faq.a: The route from La Digue to Curieuse is inside the inner-island lagoon, sheltered most of the year. Crossings rarely exceed 30 minutes.

coco-island.title: Coco Island Marine Park & the Sister Islands
coco-island.lead: A private boat circuit through the wildest snorkeling spot of the inner islands. Three granite islets, glass-clear water, a constellation of reef fish that look painted on, and beach stops most visitors never reach.
coco-island.imageAlt: Coconut palms and pink granite at a deserted Seychelles beach
coco-island.metaTitle: Coco Island & Sister Islands Tour · Snorkeling from La Digue
coco-island.metaDescription: Private boat tour to Coco Island Marine Park, Félicité and Sister Islands. Glass-clear snorkeling, deserted beaches, beach BBQ. From €130 / person, drinks included.
coco-island.schemaName: Coco Island & Sister Islands Private Boat Tour from La Digue

sections.title: Coco Island Marine Park. the inner islands' jewel
sections.body:
Coco is a small group of granite rocks off Félicité, surrounded by a marine park that has been protected for decades. The reef is just metres below the surface, the water is glass-flat in the lee of the rocks, and the fish density is honestly the best around La Digue. Expect parrotfish in every colour, sergeant majors in shoals, the resident hawksbill turtles, and on the lucky day eagle rays cruising the drop-off.

We time the morning drop on the slack tide. visibility is at its best and the current is at its lowest. Children under 12 enter the park free; adults pay the marine park fee on arrival to the ranger.

sections.title: Lunch on Grande Soeur
sections.body:
Grande Soeur is the larger of the two Sister Islands. a single beach with a leaning palm tree, no resort, no boat traffic outside the few private charters that come ashore. Lunch is a beach barbecue cooked while you swim. The water on the bay side is shallow enough to wade out 50 metres without losing your footing.

If you want a longer beach session, we trade snorkel time for it. that's the point of the private day.

sections.title: Félicité, Petite Soeur and the granite scenery
sections.body: The circuit continues past Félicité. half private island, half Six Senses estate, with cliffs that drop 80 metres into deep water and the kind of granite shapes that made the Seychelles famous. Petite Soeur is the smaller twin: a narrow strip of white sand backed by a forest you can't enter. We swing close for the photo opportunity, then anchor for a last swim on the return.

sections.title: What makes this day different from the Curieuse circuit
sections.body: If Curieuse is about land. the tortoises, the trail, the history. Coco is about the water. The snorkeling is denser, the islands are smaller and emptier, the day is more about being in the sea than walking on it. Many guests do both on a 2-day stay; we offer a small repeat-guest courtesy on the second booking.

coco-island.highlightsTitle: What's included in your Coco day
highlights: Snorkeling at the inner islands' richest reef
Beach BBQ lunch on Grande Soeur
Local captain · 12+ years on these waters
coco-island.itineraryEyebrow: A day in the marine park

faq.q: Is the Coco Marine Park fee included?
faq.a: No. it is paid in cash to the ranger on arrival (currently around €15 per adult, free for under 12s). Our captain handles the formalities.

faq.q: How is the snorkeling compared to Curieuse?
faq.a: Coco has higher fish density and deeper drops, Curieuse has more variety of corals and the chance of tortoises on the beach. Both are excellent; many guests pick Coco for the water and Curieuse for the land.

faq.q: Can we land on Sister Islands?
faq.a: Yes. Grande Soeur is open to private visits via a small private fee paid on the beach. Petite Soeur is a viewing-only stop from the boat.

faq.q: Will we see turtles?
faq.a: Sightings are common around the marine park. hawksbills on the reef shelves, very occasionally a green turtle in deeper water.

faq.q: Is this trip suitable for non-swimmers?
faq.a: Yes. The lagoon side of Grande Soeur is shallow and calm, and we provide flotation gear for the snorkel stops.

sister-islands.title: Sister Islands. Grande Soeur, Petite Soeur & Félicité
sister-islands.lead: Two granite islets off Félicité, a single deserted beach you can land on, and the kind of empty bay that makes you forget anyone else uses these waters. The Sister Islands are the inner archipelago's best-kept private day.
sister-islands.imageAlt: Granite rocks and white sand on the Sister Islands, Seychelles
sister-islands.metaTitle: Sister Islands Tour Seychelles · Grande Soeur Boat from La Digue
sister-islands.metaDescription: Private boat day to Grande Soeur and Petite Soeur from La Digue. Beach BBQ, snorkeling, Félicité passage. €130/person · drinks & lunch included.
sister-islands.schemaName: Sister Islands. Private Boat Day from La Digue

sections.title: Why the Sister Islands are the connoisseur's pick
sections.body:
Grande Soeur and Petite Soeur sit a couple of kilometres east of Félicité. granite twins with a single beach between them, no road, no jetty, no resort. Most boats pass them on their way to Coco. We make them the destination.

The west bay of Grande Soeur is one of the quietest landings of the inner islands. The water is glass-flat in the lee of the rock, the sand is the same blinding white as Anse Source d'Argent, and the bay is small enough that one boat takes the whole place. A small landing fee is paid to the island staff on arrival. they keep the trail and the bay clean.

sections.title: What you'll do on a Sister Islands day
sections.body:
Mornings on the east coast for the snorkeling. the reef shelves off Petite Soeur are alive with sergeant majors, parrotfish and the resident hawksbills. Lunch is a beach barbecue cooked while you swim. Afternoons we walk the trail across Grande Soeur if you want. it's twenty minutes of granite-and-jungle climb to a viewpoint over Félicité.

If you prefer water over walking, we trade the trail for a second snorkel stop on the way home.

sections.title: Félicité passage and the granite scenery
sections.body: On the way out and back, we run close to Félicité. the larger neighbour, half private, half Six Senses estate. Its cliffs fall straight into 80 metres of water and the granite shapes are the most dramatic in the inner islands. We don't land (no public access) but we hold the boat off the south point for the photo and a swim if conditions allow.

sections.title: Sister Islands vs Coco. which one to pick?
sections.body: If you want intensity in the water, choose Coco. more fish, more current, a tighter marine park. If you want a beach to yourself, choose Sister Islands. Many guests do Coco one day and Sister Islands the next; we offer a small repeat-guest courtesy on the second booking.

sister-islands.highlightsTitle: What's included on your Sister Islands day
highlights: Optional trail walk across Grande Soeur
sister-islands.itineraryEyebrow: A day on the Sister Islands

faq.q: Is there a landing fee on Grande Soeur?
faq.a: Yes, a small fee paid in cash on the beach to the island staff (currently around €15 per adult, free for children under 12). It maintains the trail and the bay.

faq.q: Can we walk between Grande Soeur and Petite Soeur?
faq.a: No. they are separated by a shallow channel that you can swim across at low tide, but it's not always safe due to current. The captain will advise on the day.

faq.q: Is the beach really private?
faq.a: Most days yes. A handful of private charters pass through; mass-tourism boats don't make this stop. If another boat is in the bay, we move to the east beach.

faq.q: Can we land on Petite Soeur?
faq.a: It's a viewing-only stop. no landing. We anchor close enough for great photos and a swim.

faq.q: Is the trail family-friendly?
faq.a: Yes. twenty minutes of gradual climb on a marked path. Solid shoes recommended; we provide reef-safe footwear if you didn't pack any.

anse-lazio.title: Anse Lazio by Boat. The Beach Seen from the Water
anse-lazio.lead: The most photographed beach of Praslin, approached the way it deserves. from the water, where you see the curve of the bay, the granite shoulders, and the reef shelf that makes Lazio's lagoon the impossible turquoise of every postcard.
anse-lazio.imageAlt: Turquoise water and granite at Anse Lazio, Praslin, Seychelles
anse-lazio.metaTitle: Anse Lazio Boat Tour · Praslin from the Sea (Master Boat Charter)
anse-lazio.metaDescription: Half-day private boat to Anse Lazio from La Digue. Approach by sea, anchor swim, snorkeling on the north reef, optional Anse Georgette stop. €130/person.
anse-lazio.schemaName: Anse Lazio Private Boat Half-Day from La Digue

sections.title: Why Anse Lazio is better from the water
sections.body:
Anse Lazio is regularly ranked among the most beautiful beaches in the world. By road you arrive at one end of it, walk through the trees and step onto the sand. By boat you see the whole curve at once. the granite shoulders that frame the bay, the reef bar a hundred metres off the beach, the colour gradient from turquoise to ink-blue as the depth drops.

We anchor inside the bay, give you the option to swim ashore (no entry fee from the water), and use the north reef for the snorkel stop. It's the best way to see this beach without sharing it with every road tourist on Praslin.

sections.title: The reef on the north side
sections.body: The north end of Anse Lazio has a granite outcrop that drops straight into 5-8 metres of clear water. The reef on that face is alive with parrotfish, butterflyfish, the occasional eagle ray and a resident pair of hawksbill turtles. It's one of the most consistent snorkel stops on the west side of Praslin. visibility is best on the morning tide.

sections.title: Optional stop at Anse Georgette
sections.body: If conditions allow, we add a short stop at Anse Georgette on the return. Georgette is technically inside the Constance Lemuria resort but accessible from the sea. most boats can't anchor there because of the reef, but we know the line in. It's emptier than Lazio and feels half a degree more remote.

sections.title: Anse Lazio vs the La Digue tour. which to pick?
sections.body: Pick Anse Lazio if you want a half-day in the most famous beach of Praslin without the road crowds. Pick the La Digue tour if you'd rather spend the time around your own island and see Anse Source d'Argent from the sea. Both work as half-day options; we run them in the morning or the afternoon, and Lazio is one of our best-rated sunset alternatives.

highlights: Snorkel stop on the north reef
anse-lazio.itineraryEyebrow: Half a day at Anse Lazio

faq.q: Is there an entry fee to Anse Lazio?
faq.a: Not from the sea. The road access is free; if you swim in from the boat, you simply step onto the public beach.

faq.q: Can we land at Anse Georgette?
faq.a: Officially the beach belongs to the Constance Lemuria resort, but it is open to the public from the sea. We can approach by boat and swim ashore depending on conditions.

faq.q: Is the bay safe for children?
faq.a: Yes. the lagoon side is shallow and protected. The reef on the north side is for confident swimmers.

faq.q: What about the south-east trade winds?
faq.a: From June to September the south-easters can make Lazio choppy in the afternoon. We adapt. morning slot is safer.

faq.q: Can we combine Anse Lazio with St-Pierre Islet?
faq.a: Yes, often. The two are 15 minutes apart by boat. many guests do both as a full-day combo.

st-pierre-islet.title: St-Pierre Islet. The Best Snorkeling Off Praslin
st-pierre-islet.lead: A granite outcrop the size of a tennis court, surrounded by a coral garden you can drift over in 4 metres of glass-flat water. St-Pierre is the inner islands' shortest, densest snorkel. and our most-requested half-day.
st-pierre-islet.imageAlt: Granite outcrop of St-Pierre Islet near Praslin, Seychelles
st-pierre-islet.metaTitle: St-Pierre Islet Snorkeling Tour Seychelles · Half-Day Private Boat
st-pierre-islet.metaDescription: Half-day boat tour from La Digue to St-Pierre Islet. one of the richest snorkeling sites near Praslin. €70/person, drinks & gear included.
st-pierre-islet.schemaName: St-Pierre Islet. Private Boat Snorkel Tour from La Digue

sections.title: Why St-Pierre is the best half-day in the inner islands
sections.body:
St-Pierre is a single granite outcrop off Anse Volbert. about a kilometre offshore, surrounded on three sides by a healthy coral garden in 3-5 metres of water. The fish density is, honestly, the highest you'll see on the inner-island side of Praslin: thick shoals of sergeant majors, parrotfish in every colour, often a hawksbill turtle resting on the bottom.

We drop on the south face for the soft current and the wider reef, drift north on the changing tide, and pick you up on the back side. The whole stop runs about 90 minutes. long enough to see everything, short enough that no one tires.

sections.title: Combining St-Pierre with Anse Volbert
sections.body: On the way back, we add a beach stop at Anse Volbert. Praslin's main beach on the Côte d'Or, a long arc of white sand with the lagoon hotels on one side and the boats moored on the other. Swim, walk, grab a coconut from the kiosk. Many guests use it as a lunch stop before returning to La Digue.

sections.title: When the visibility is at its best
sections.body: St-Pierre is good year-round but the sweet spot is between April and October. light south-east winds, low rainfall, visibility often above 15 metres. December-February can be excellent on calm days but more variable. The captain checks the forecast the morning of and shifts the plan if needed.

sections.title: St-Pierre vs Coco Marine Park
sections.body: Coco has more fish density and a larger area, but it's a longer day and requires the marine park fee. St-Pierre is shorter, free of park fees, and the density at the actual outcrop rivals Coco. If you have one half-day, pick St-Pierre. If you have a full day, Coco wins.

st-pierre-islet.highlightsTitle: What's included in the St-Pierre half-day

faq.q: Is there a marine park fee at St-Pierre?
faq.a: No. St-Pierre itself sits outside the gazetted parks. No daily fee is required.

faq.q: How deep is the water at the snorkel site?
faq.a: Between 3 and 8 metres around the islet. shallower on the south face, dropping off to 12 m past the back of the rock.

faq.q: Can children snorkel here?
faq.a: Yes. flotation gear available, the south face is shallow and protected, the captain stays close in the dinghy if needed.

faq.q: Can we land on St-Pierre?
faq.a: It's bare granite. no path, no facilities. We don't land. Snorkel only.

faq.q: Can we combine with Curieuse?
faq.a: Yes. it adds about an hour and turns the day into a full-day Curieuse + St-Pierre combo. Very popular.

sunset-cruise.title: La Digue Sunset Cruise. The Last Light of the Day
sunset-cruise.tagline: Anse Source d'Argent at golden hour · drinks · private
sunset-cruise.lead: Three hours on the water at the only time the inner islands turn gold. We board at 16:30, slide along La Digue's east coast, hold the boat off Anse Source d'Argent for the sunset, and drift back into the marina under the last colour of the day.
sunset-cruise.imageAlt: Master Boat Charter at sunset around La Digue, Seychelles
sunset-cruise.metaTitle: La Digue Sunset Cruise · Private Boat at Golden Hour Seychelles
sunset-cruise.metaDescription: Private sunset cruise from La Digue. Anse Source d'Argent at golden hour, drinks, platter onboard. €70/person · 3 hours · 10 guests max.
sunset-cruise.schemaName: La Digue Sunset Cruise. Private Boat at Golden Hour

sections.title: Why the inner islands are at their best at sunset
sections.body:
Sunset in Seychelles is short. twenty minutes from gold to dark. but those twenty minutes are what people travel for. The granite of La Digue, pink in afternoon light, turns orange and then deep red. The lagoon goes from turquoise to pewter. The reef cuts a darker line on the water. From the boat, with the engine off, the only sound is the swell against the hull.

We time the cruise to the exact sun angle of the day. boarding at 16:30, holding off Anse Source d'Argent between 17:30 and 18:00, returning to marina between 19:00 and 19:30 depending on the month.

sections.title: Anse Source d'Argent at golden hour
sections.body: The land park closes at 18:00. From the sea, the beach stays open as long as you can see it. We hold the boat 80 metres offshore. close enough that the granite shapes feel three storeys tall, far enough that the wash doesn't bother anyone still on the beach. If the tide is right, you can step off the boat and walk to the sand. Most guests just stay onboard with a drink and watch.

sections.title: What's onboard
sections.body: A chilled bottle (you choose at booking. sparkling, white, rosé or non-alcoholic), water, sodas, and a small platter. local fruit, cheese, light bites. The captain keeps the engine low and the route smooth. No microphone, no group banter. it's your evening.

sections.title: The honeymoon version
sections.body: If you book the sunset for an occasion (honeymoon, anniversary, proposal), tell us. We add a small surprise. flowers from the local market, a card from the captain, a slightly longer route past Petite Anse where almost no other boats go. We do this discreetly; no surprise mention on the boat itself.

sunset-cruise.highlightsTitle: What's included in the sunset cruise
highlights: Anse Source d'Argent from the water at golden hour
Optional anchor stop for a swim
Slow cruise back to the marina

faq.q: What time does the cruise start?
faq.a: Boarding at 16:30. we adjust by 30 minutes either way depending on the month and the actual sunset time. We'll confirm the exact time the day before.

faq.q: Can we book this for a proposal or honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes. tell us at booking and we'll add a small surprise (flowers, captain's card, slightly longer route). It stays discreet.

faq.q: Is there food onboard?
faq.a: A small platter (fruit, cheese, light bites) and drinks. For a full dinner we recommend the marina restaurants on return.

faq.q: What if the weather is cloudy?
faq.a: If forecast looks completely overcast, we offer a free reschedule. Light cloud often makes the colours more dramatic. we'll be honest the morning of.

faq.q: Can we swim during the cruise?
faq.a: Yes, weather allowing. usually a short stop at Anse Source d'Argent or Petite Anse. Bring swimwear.

la-digue-tour.title: Around La Digue by Sea. Anse Source d'Argent from the Water
la-digue-tour.tagline: Anse Source d'Argent · Anse Cocos · Grande Anse
la-digue-tour.lead: Half a day or sunset around La Digue, seen the way the island was always meant to be seen. from the water. We slip along the granite shore, anchor where no road reaches, and finish on the cliff-side beaches at golden hour.
la-digue-tour.imageAlt: Master Boat Charter cruising past the granite cliffs of La Digue, Seychelles
la-digue-tour.metaTitle: La Digue Boat Tour · Anse Source d'Argent from the Sea
la-digue-tour.metaDescription: Private half-day or sunset boat tour around La Digue: Anse Source d'Argent from the water, Anse Cocos, Grande Anse, Petite Anse. €70 / person, drinks included.
la-digue-tour.schemaName: La Digue Private Boat Tour. Beaches & Sunset Cruise

sections.title: Why the best view of La Digue is from the boat
sections.body:
Most visitors see La Digue from a bicycle saddle. which is good, but partial. The island's true silhouette is its 9 kilometres of granite coastline, the cliffs that fall straight into deep water on the east side, the sea-only beaches at Anse Cocos and Petite Anse, and Anse Source d'Argent at sunset when the road is closed but the water is open.

We run two versions of this trip. A morning circuit with two anchorages and a swim. A sunset circuit that times Anse Source d'Argent for the golden hour and finishes back in the marina under a sky most people only see in postcards.

sections.title: Anse Source d'Argent from the water
sections.body:
From the sea, Anse Source d'Argent reveals what you can't see from the path: the long curve of granite shoulders behind the famous palm tree, the offshore reef shelf that turns the lagoon turquoise, and. at low tide. a sandbank where you can step off the boat into 30 cm of water and walk to the beach.

The park has an entry fee on the land side; from the water we simply anchor offshore and you swim in if you like.

sections.title: Anse Cocos and the east-coast beaches
sections.body: Anse Cocos is one of those Seychelles beaches that has no easy land access. a long walk from Grande Anse or a short swim from the boat. Same for Petite Anse: a sliver of sand framed by two granite shoulders, with a single house behind it. We anchor in the lee, you swim or snorkel; the captain stays with the boat.

sections.title: The sunset version of this trip
sections.body: Booked between 16:30 and 19:30 depending on season. We start by heading south down the east coast, swing back past Anse Source d'Argent for the gold light, then drift slowly into the marina under the last colour of the day. Drinks, a small platter on board, and the kind of quiet you don't get on a group cruise.

highlights: Choice of morning or sunset slot
Photo stops at Anse Source d'Argent from the sea
la-digue-tour.itineraryEyebrow: Half a day around the island

faq.q: Can we land at Anse Source d'Argent?
faq.a: Yes. you swim ashore from the anchored boat at low tide it is barely a wade. The land park fee is only required if you walk further inland.

faq.q: Sunset cruise vs morning cruise. which to pick?
faq.a: Sunset for the light and the calm. Morning if you want the longer swim and snorkel windows.

faq.q: Is this trip good for honeymooners?
faq.a: Many guests book it for a private anniversary. We can add a small platter, a chilled bottle, and a slower pace if you let us know.

faq.q: Will we see other boats?
faq.a: On the Anse Source d'Argent stretch, sometimes one or two. Past the south point, almost never.

faq.q: Is the sea calm year-round?
faq.a: Inside La Digue it is calm most of the year. On the east coast the south-east trade winds (June-September) bring some swell. we adapt the route.

captainPage.lead: A single boat. A single captain. A single group at a time. The Seychellois behind Master Boat Charter explains, in his own words, what that means and why he runs it this way.

sections.title: Born on the right rock
sections.body: Born in La Digue, raised between the marina and the reef. School on the island until the secondary years on Praslin, then the family boats. fishing the inner banks with his father from his early teens. The kind of life where you know the names of more fish than streets.

sections.title: From fishing to charter
sections.body: After years of commercial fishing, he saw the way mass tourism was handling these islands and decided he'd rather do less and do it well. One boat. Local. Direct. The first private charter day was years ago. same captain, same boat, just more guests now.

sections.title: Why one boat
sections.body: "If I run two boats, I'm a manager. I'm on the phone, I'm doing logistics, I'm not on the water with my guests. If I run one boat, I'm a captain. I know everyone on board, I cook the lunch, I read the weather, I choose the reef. That's what I want to be."

sections.title: What he wants you to know
sections.body: Tell us what matters most to you. Tortoises? We'll plan around Curieuse. Snorkeling? We'll pick the reef on the morning tide. A quiet beach? We know which one will be empty on the day. The Seychelles are small enough that a captain who grew up here can give you a personal day, every day.

day.title: What a full day on the Master looks like.
day.lead: A typical full-day excursion. Times shift with the weather, the tide and your wishes. that's the whole point of going private.

steps.body: Pickup at the jetty. Briefing, life jackets, snorkeling gear fitted. Coffee onboard.

steps.title: First snorkeling stop
steps.body: A protected reef chosen by your captain that morning, based on visibility and current. Turtles, reef fish, corals.

steps.title: Castaway island
steps.body: Walk, swim, climb the granite. A beach with no other boats in sight when possible.

steps.title: Lunch ashore
steps.body: Barbecue on a quiet beach: grilled fish, salads, fresh fruit. Drinks included. Half-day guests disembark here.

steps.title: Second snorkeling or swim
steps.body: Another reef, a quiet anchorage, or a long swim in glass-flat water.

steps.title: Return to La Digue
steps.body: Slow ride back. The light at this hour is what people remember.

sections.title: Booking & payment

items.q: How do I book a boat tour with Master Boat Charter?
items.a: Pick a date and a slot on the booking page (about 2 minutes). You'll get a confirmation by email and WhatsApp within 2 hours. No card is required at this stage. payment is by bank transfer or cash on the day.

items.q: Do I need to pay in advance?
items.a: A 20% deposit is required to confirm your reservation. The remaining balance is paid on the day of the activity, by bank transfer or in cash.

Free cancellation up to 72 hours before departure. Within 72 hours we propose a reschedule subject to availability. If the captain cancels for weather reasons, a full refund or free reschedule is always offered.

items.q: How quickly do you confirm a booking?
items.a: Express confirmation during operating hours (8 AM to 8 PM Seychelles time, UTC+4), usually within a few minutes by WhatsApp.

items.q: Can I book a private group of 12 or more?
items.a: Our boat holds 10 guests. For larger parties we coordinate with a partner boat. message the captain on WhatsApp and we'll arrange it.

sections.title: On the boat

items.a: Yes. a marine toilet with a door, for all guests.
Drinks (water, soft drinks, beer) are included on every trip. Full-day excursions include a beach barbecue. grilled fish, salads, fresh fruit. For specific dietary needs, tell us at booking.
Yes. masks, snorkels and fins in all sizes. Bring your own if you prefer.

items.q: Is the boat covered from the sun?
items.a: Yes, a full T-top covers the cockpit. The bow is open for swimmers and sun lovers.
No, but the captain carries a mobile hotspot for emergencies and shared photos.

sections.title: Wildlife, weather & practical

items.a: Very often. hawksbill turtles are present year-round at our snorkeling sites around Curieuse, Coco and St-Pierre. Greens nest seasonally on protected beaches.

items.q: When can we see whale sharks?
items.a: August to October is the peak season around the inner islands. Outside that window sightings are rare; the captain will be honest if it's not the right time.
Inside the inner islands the sea is generally calm and protected. For big game fishing the swell is larger. we advise based on the day's forecast and can adapt the route.
Yes. The boat is family-friendly, with life jackets in every size and shaded areas. Tell us the ages of children at booking and we'll prepare accordingly.

items.q: What happens if the weather is bad?
items.a: We reschedule at no cost, or refund in full if no alternative date works. The captain decides based on safety, not bookings.
Reef-safe sunscreen, towel, swimwear, hat, a light layer for the return. We provide everything else. snorkeling gear, drinks, food on full-day trips, flotation gear, first aid.
We operate from La Digue to visit every inner island: Praslin, Mahé, Curieuse, Cousin, Coco Island, Grande Soeur, Petite Soeur, Félicité, St Pierre and more.

items.q: Why is there only one boat?
items.a: It's a choice. One boat means we can keep groups small, the experience personal and our impact on the marine environment low. Every guest gets our full attention.
Drinks are included on every trip. Food is included depending on the package: full-day excursions include a beach barbecue, fishing trips include snacks. Specific menus can be tailored on request.
A 20% deposit confirms your booking. The balance is paid on the day of the activity, by bank transfer or in cash.
No. Marine park fees (for sites such as Curieuse, Saint Pierre, Coco) are paid locally and not included in the rate.
Free cancellation up to 72 hours before departure. Inside 72 hours, the slot remains reserved for you and rescheduling is offered subject to availability.

items.q: Is the boat suitable for children?
items.a: Absolutely. The boat is family-friendly with shade, toilets onboard and flotation gear in every size. Tell us your group composition and we'll prepare accordingly.
Inside the Seychelles inner islands the sea is generally calm and protected. For game fishing the swell is larger. we'll advise based on the day's conditions.
Booking online is reservation only. no card needed at this stage. We'll confirm by email and WhatsApp and arrange payment by bank transfer or cash on the day.

longDescription.title: Why choose Master Boat Charter?
longDescription.intro: Master Boat Charter is the reference for boat excursions and rentals in Seychelles. From our base in La Digue we run unforgettable days in the most beautiful lagoons of the archipelago.
longDescription.block1: Our captain is Seychellois and passionate about his island. He knows the secret spots: wild coves, deserted islets, untouched reefs. Far more than a ride, a true authentic experience.
longDescription.block2: Whether you want a private boat with skipper, a snorkeling outing, a sunset cruise, or a quick island transfer, our fleet adapts to your wishes. Every boat is regularly inspected for safety and comfort.
longDescription.block3: We are committed to sustainable tourism in Seychelles. Our excursions are designed to minimise environmental impact: no anchoring on coral, low-waste practices, marine wildlife awareness.
longDescription.block4: Pick your date, pick your activity and book directly online. Our smart calendar prevents double bookings, and confirmation is handled personally by our team.
longDescription.block5: Want a picnic on a deserted beach? A swim stop in a turquoise lagoon? A guided visit to Curieuse, Saint-Pierre or Félicité? Every outing is shaped around your wishes for unforgettable memories.
longDescription.outro: Book your excursion now and explore the marine treasures of the Seychelles with Master Boat Charter. your partner at sea.

about.title: A single boat. A whole archipelago.
about.lead: Master Boat Charter is a small, local operation built on a simple idea: do less, do it well, and leave the sea exactly as you found it.
about.story: We started with one boat, a deep love for these waters, and a frustration with how mass tourism was handling them. Years later, the boat is the same. So is the approach. What's grown is the trust. from guests who come back, and from local guides and captains who choose to work with us.
